notes: Fix equivalent to the reference with inline Quoted checks and updated doc comments; tests are extensive, but it rewrites an existing snippet test's fixture and expectations, and adds a brittle exact-JSON httpcaddyfile test.
Same correct fix with updated doc comments and extensive new tests, though it rewrites an existing snippet test's inputs and expectations and adds a fairly heavy httpcaddyfile matrix.

Production changes match the reference everywhere it matters (dispenser NextArg/NextBlock/ArgErr, parser addresses, directives, doImport, directive, open/close curly brace checks, blockTokens), though it uses inline `.Quoted()` checks rather than helpers, and tests cover all three quote styles at the dispenser, parser, import and integration-adapt levels.
Matches the reference semantics at every brace-check site, using inline `!Token().Quoted()` instead of helpers, and adds thorough dispenser, parser, import and caddyfile-adapt integration tests.

Same coverage of every brace check as the reference, with an equivalent `if !token.Quoted()` wrapper in doImport, but it leaves the NextArg and RemainingArgs doc comments stale; tests are thorough, including a quoted site key and imported snippet args.

Functionally equivalent to the reference, with doImport's switch wrapped in a quoted guard, but leaves the doc comments unchanged; it adds broad tests covering quote styles, nesting, NextSegment, quoted keys and snippet args.

Returning all same-module import statements per ConfigResource fixes the reported for_each/count drop, and the unit and integration tests are thorough; but parent precedence still applies per resource rather than per instance, so a child module's import for a different instance is silently dropped whenever the parent imports any instance of that resource.

Keeping every same-module import block per ConfigResource fixes the reported for_each/count case. However, a parent block still overrides all of a child's blocks for that resource, so a child's import of a different instance is silently dropped, unlike the reference's per-instance dedup.

Same map-of-slices fix as C1, with a slightly more defensive TargetContains ancestor check; it fixes the issue's scenario but keeps whole-resource override, so a parent that imports one instance still silently discards child imports for other instances, and the only new test is the basic issue repro.

Takes essentially the same approach as C1 with a more convoluted ancestor check (TargetContains loop). It has the same flaw: a parent block overrides all child blocks for the resource rather than per instance, so partial parent overrides silently drop child imports. It adds only a single for_each test.

Leaves FindImportStatements deduplicating to one 'representative' and then re-scans the module config in findImportTargets to recover the discarded blocks, which leaks refactoring logic into the caller; behaviour matches C1/C2, including the same partial parent/child override gap, though its table test covers count, for_each imports, child modules and full override.

Keeps the lossy one-representative-per-resource dedup and has the caller re-scan the module config to recover the dropped blocks, which leaks the abstraction. It shares the same parent-overrides-whole-resource limitation, though its tests are broad (count, for_each imports, child module, full parent override).
